name: Stefan Harrer, PhD
headline: VP, Global Head of R&D Data and Computational Sciences
summary:
AI innovator. Systems creator. Builder of impact from thin air.

I turn bold ideas into real-world impact—prototypes, MVPs, programs, IP. As a scientist and executive, I build frontier AI systems and deploy them at scale in complex, high-stakes environments across biotech, pharma, MedTech, and digital health.

Today, I serve as VP and Global Head of R&D Data and Computational Sciences at Sanofi, where I lead the global computational and data science agenda across the company’s digital R&D organization. My focus is embedding advanced data science, AI, and in-silico approaches into the entire drug discovery and development stack to accelerate breakthroughs and bring new medicines to patients faster. 

Previously, as Director of AI for Science at CSIRO, Australia’s National Science Agency, I co-founded and led a $39M program (in collaboration with Google Research) to reinvent scientific discovery using generative AI agents. The flagship platform, Sciansa, which we built and deployed is a multi-agent lab assistant helping thousands of scientists accelerate scientific discovery across biology, robotics, and other domains. 

Earlier at IBM Research, I founded the Brain-Inspired Computing Program and launched IBM’s global epilepsy program. Our team built the first AI capable of predicting epileptic seizures in real time using wearable technology—work that ultimately seeded Australia’s first MedTech startup valued at over $100M. 

I’m a TEDx speaker, IBM Master Inventor with 76 granted patents, and was inducted to IBM's Academy of Technology, to IBM's Health and Life Sciences Research Council, and to the New York Academy of Sciences. I publish widely in journals and conference proceedings of The Lancet, Nature, JAMA, Cell, NeurIPS, IJCAI, AAAI, MICCAI, CVPR, ACM, and IEEE. You'll find my work featured in WIRED, Forbes, ABC, the WHO, FierceBiotech, and the World Economic Forum. 

I believe in building AI that matters—and backing up every idea with flawless, inclusive and relentless execution.

The HBR Advisory Council provides feedback to HBR editors, previews new content, and comments on ideas from HBR as well as those from the wider world of management and leadership.
